evidence.quoted_text:
def atomic(filename, data):
    filename = Path(filename)
    durable_directory(filename.parent)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=filename.parent, delete=False) as stream:
        stream.write(data)
        stream.flush()
        os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        temporary = stream.name
    os.replace(temporary, filename)
    fsync_dir(filename.parent)
evidence.reason: At the pinned tip, `atomic` creates a `delete=False` staging file and has no try/finally cleanup. If `stream.write`/`flush`, `os.fsync`, or `os.replace` raises, the named temporary file stays in the artifact/master directory; retries create additional unreachable files, and repeated failures (e.g. disk-full or I/O errors while `ArtifactStore.put` writes bytes) can consume space needed for recovery. The current code also assigns `temporary` only after `fsync`, so a failure before that point cannot be cleaned up by the caller. This is an ordinary minor error-path defect, not a new requirement, and the fix (capture the path before writing, unlink it in a finally on failure, keep the post-replace directory fsync) is routine. Note the finding's recorded intervals [381,386] point at unrelated payload-import validation; the actual `atomic` implementation is at lines 419-428.
